director.question: q3
director.why: q3 offers the most bits and a near-certain no that would refute the leading fading models if violated

question.text: Brighter in r three days from now than at its last r detection?

risky.text: Brighter than 80 microjansky in r 5 days from now?

payload.rule: Every ZTF g or r measurement taken after this bet was sealed, up to one day past its last forecast, is scored against the forecast, interpolated linearly between days. The question is settled by the first r measurement within a day of its time; a limit above the reference leaves it void.

instrument.why: Five r-band detections spanning 20 days show a slow consistent fade with repeatable photometry and a high real stamp score.

theories.argument: The r band light curve fades slowly over twenty days and matches a low redshift Type II template with chi squared per point well below one. The candidate is a high confidence real point source on a galaxy disk far from the Galactic plane consistent with a massive star collapse.

refuted_if.why: A hydrogen rich plateau about thirty five days after peak should still hold near current brightness in r so a halving within three days would break the plateau expectation.

theories.weakest_point: No color information exists and a seventeen day gap leaves the decline shape poorly sampled with only r band detections.

theories.argument: The r-band rise into the fitted maximum at -18.4 d at z=0.082 with normal color c=-0.03 and excellent chi2 of 0.24 matches a Type Ia peak near 18.6 mag. The later r detections near 19.2 mag about 15 d after peak match the expected post-maximum decline of a fast-declining Ia on its radioactive tail.

refuted_if.why: A fast-declining Ia more than twenty days past peak must keep fading below the current plateau and cannot remain this bright without continued power beyond nickel decay.

theories.weakest_point: The fit forces x1 near minus three at the extreme fast-decliner edge with only r-band data and a seventeen-day gap, so there is no color confirmation and the flat three-day plateau is atypical for suc

theories.argument: The r-band fading from ~127 uJy at day -20.5 to ~69 uJy at day -0.5 matches a post-maximum stripped-envelope tail at z=0.16 peaking near day -40 with chi2 per point 0.21. The slow decline of about 0.03 mag per day at high Galactic latitude with a real PSF is consistent with cobalt-powered Ib/c ejecta.

refuted_if.why: A fading cobalt tail predicts about 55 uJy by day 5 so sustained brightness would rule out the model.

theories.weakest_point: The case rests on r-band only with a 17-day gap and no observed peak or color, so phase and redshift are extrapolated and rival weights exceed Ib/c.

wording.text: It is very unlikely that the distant flash will still be shining brightly in red light 5 days from now.
